## ✨ Highlights

- 🔒 **Consul 2.1.0 for the nodes with the Consul extension**: the agent is built with a newer Go, whose standard library fixes one critical and nine high vulnerabilities (`net/http`, `net/textproto`, `crypto/tls`).
- 🐧 **Linux 7.2.13 and 6.18.59**: both kernel tracks follow their upstream stable releases; 6.18.59 fixes a high-rated UDP side channel for the nodes pinned to the longterm track.
- ⚡ **Proxmox machines get AES-NI**: the Controller now creates its Proxmox VE machines with the `x86-64-v2-AES` CPU model, not the API's `kvm64` - HAProxy's TLS is back on AES-GCM and on the processor's fast code for every curve and hash ([#379](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/379)). Machines created before keep `kvm64` until changed by hand (⚠️ below).
- 🔐 **Let's Encrypt doesn't wait five minutes after a HAProxy change**: an HTTP-01 order that fails while HAProxy's configuration is being applied is tried again at once ([#381](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/381)).
- 🤖 **The janusctl plugin has its icon**: Claude Code shows Janus's tile for the `janusctl` plugin ([#367](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/367)) - `claude plugin update janusctl@janus` takes it ([Claude Code and janusctl](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/claude-code.md)).

## 🔒 Security

For **nodes with the Consul extension** ([Consul](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/consul.md)):

- **Consul 2.1.0** (was 2.0.4), HashiCorp's release binary, its checksum list checked against HashiCorp's release key. Built with Go 1.26.10 and `golang.org/x/net` 0.60.0, which fix:
  - 🔴 critical: `net/http` - [CVE-2026-78663](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6612) (HTTP/2 server streams refund flow control twice);
  - 🟠 high: `net/http` - [CVE-2026-56866](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6605) (client connection desynchronization after a refused `CONNECT`), [CVE-2026-94439](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6613) (server connection desynchronization after a 2xx `CONNECT`), [CVE-2026-78667](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6609) (no limit on the size of parsed `Range` headers), [CVE-2026-78659](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6603) (HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion through trailers), [CVE-2026-78660](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6610) (HTTP/2 transport accepting malformed framing headers), [CVE-2026-78669](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611) (CPU exhaustion from repeated initial window changes), [CVE-2026-97032](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6617) (HTTP/2 server crash in the HPACK encoder); `net/textproto`, `mime/multipart` - [CVE-2026-94440](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6608) (memory limit bypassed parsing MIME headers); `crypto/tls` - [CVE-2026-97031](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6607) (malformed ECH outer extension references);
  - 🟡 medium: `html/template` - [CVE-2026-94448](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6599), [CVE-2026-97030](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6600);
  - and [CVE-2026-111943](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6809) (`crypto/x509`, compromised intermediate certificates), which v2026.10.21 fixed in Janus's own binaries.

  The agent's HTTP API answers on `127.0.0.1:8500` only, so its HTTP server's fixes matter from the node itself; its HTTP health checks use the fixed client. Update the nodes that run it.

For **nodes on the longterm kernel track** (a schematic with `"kernel": "longterm"`):

- **Linux 6.18.59** (was 6.18.58): 🟠 high [CVE-2026-99077](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99077) - an off-path attacker could learn the ephemeral port of a connected UDP socket through the route exception cache (ICMP "fragmentation needed" and redirects quoting a UDP packet). Two more CVEs fixed in this release touch files Janus's kernel doesn't build. The default track has had the fix since Linux 7.2.11.

## ⚙️ Node

- **Linux 7.2.13** for the default kernel track (was 7.2.12) and **6.18.59** for the longterm one (was 6.18.58), each from its signature-checked source, the configuration unchanged. 7.2.13 fixes no known vulnerability among the files Janus's kernel builds; 6.18.59's is above.
- **HAProxy on AWS-LC 5.12.0** (was 5.11.0), every branch: hardening upstream - OCSP, ASN.1 and RSA-PSS checks, a small set of intermediate certificates blocked explicitly; no known vulnerability fixed.
- **Consul 2.1.0** for the Consul extension (above). Its breaking changes concern `consul connect redirect-traffic` (transparent proxying, now with nftables) and Consul Enterprise - not the client agent a node runs: its configuration doesn't change.
- **Let's Encrypt, HTTP-01** ([#381](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/381)): applying a HAProxy configuration already retried at once the HTTP-01 certificates that had failed; one being **ordered** at that moment failed afterwards - the CA checked the challenge during HAProxy's reload, or before the new frontend answered it - and waited its five-minute backoff. The node now notes HAProxy's changes during an order and retries it at once when one happened ([HTTP-01: HAProxy answers](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/letsencrypt.md#http-01-haproxy-answers)).

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Proxmox VE: the `x86-64-v2-AES` CPU model** for every machine the Controller creates ([#379](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/379)) - what Proxmox's own form gives a new machine. Without a `cpu` key, Proxmox's API made them `kvm64`: no AES-NI, SSE4, AVX, BMI2 or ADX, so AWS-LC negotiated ChaCha20 and ran generic code for P-256, X25519 and SHA-256 - and so did janusd. The model still migrates live between any x86-64-v2 hosts with AES. The token's role already had `VM.Config.CPU`. libvirt machines were not affected (`host-passthrough`). [Creating a node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/hypervisors.md#creating-a-node) lists each driver's model.
- **libvirt host preparation: the UEFI firmware** ([#378](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/378), [#384](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/384)): a new step 5 hides QEMU's firmware builds loaded into memory - AMD SEV's and Intel TDX's, no flash and no variable store. Ubuntu's `ovmf` package installs them and libvirt picked the SEV build, which AppArmor refused: a machine never started on an Ubuntu 26.04 host. A host whose KVM runs SEV or TDX guests keeps them, with a warning; Debian 13 has none to hide. polkit and Check are now steps 6 and 7, their old links still lead to them ([5. The UEFI firmware](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/hypervisors.md#5-the-uefi-firmware)).

## 🤖 Claude Code

- **The plugin's icon** ([#367](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/367)): `claude-code/janusctl/.claude-plugin/icon.png`, the brand's tile - the symbol on a dark rounded square, readable on light and dark lists; `claude plugin validate` no longer asks for one. A test keeps it equal to `brand/png/janus-tuile-1024.png`.

## 📖 Docs and site

- **A network without DHCP** ([#380](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/380)): every boot first waits about 165 s for the kernel's DHCP, a static configuration included - and a DHCP reservation of the node's static address avoids it, with a libvirt network's example ([DHCP is the kernel's, for now](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md#dhcp-is-the-kernels-for-now)).
- The [landing page](https://janus.sw-servers.net/) lists Claude Code among Janus's features ([#366](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/366)).
- The docs' screenshots wait for each page's first render before its splash leaves ([#377](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/377)): the splash, or a page missing its text, no longer gets in a shot now and then.
- The lab campaigns of [v2026.10.27-2](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.27-2.md) - `haproxy server-state` and `haproxy reload` under load, Claude Code on the lab with a reader and an operator certificate - and [v2026.10.27-3](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.27-3.md) ([#362](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/362), [#365](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/365)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- Update the nodes with the Consul extension and those pinned to the longterm kernel track (🔒 above); the others get Linux 7.2.13 and AWS-LC 5.12.0.
- **Proxmox VE machines created by an earlier Controller** keep `kvm64` (`qm config <vmid>` shows no `cpu:` line): on the host, `qm set <vmid> --cpu x86-64-v2-AES`, then stop and start the machine - a reboot from inside keeps the same QEMU process. Drain a cluster member first, one member at a time.
- **libvirt hosts on Ubuntu**: run the host preparation again (Hypervisors › the host › Show host preparation) before creating machines there. Elsewhere it changes nothing.
- janusctl and Terraform are unchanged but for the version.
